children: 1054 ET - Gains in CBOT grain futures over the past month have pushed crop prices up through the break-even levels often cited by U.S. farmers to make planted acres profitable. While this has noticeably shifted the sentiment of farmers to being more positive, analysts with the University of Missouri's Food & Agricultural Policy Research Institute say that higher input costs remain a problem for farmer finances. "Crop returns, through a combination of continued soft crop prices and elevated production costs, remain under pressure," says FAPRI in a recent report. However, the average prices assumed in FAPRI's report are well-below where futures are trading at now. CBOT grain futures are currently down, with corn off 2.5%, soybeans down 0.7%, and wheat falls 4.6%.(kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
Even With Higher Futures, Farm Returns Stay Under Pressure — Market Talk

1055 ET - Gains in CBOT grain futures over the past month have pushed crop prices up through the break-even levels often cited by U.S. farmers to make planted acres profitable. While this has noticeably shifted the sentiment of farmers to being more positive, analysts with the University of Missouri's Food & Agricultural Policy Research Institute say that higher input costs remain a problem for farmer finances. "Crop returns, through a combination of continued soft crop prices and elevated production costs, remain under pressure," says FAPRI in a recent report. However, the average prices assumed in FAPRI's report are well-below where futures are trading at now. CBOT grain futures are currently down, with corn off 2.5%, soybeans down 0.7%, and wheat falls 4.6%.(kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
